x: HSFC handles Gaganyaan mission planning and crew selection and training.

s: For which of the following is the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC) of ISRO responsible?
x: LPSC develops liquid and cryogenic stages; URSC builds satellites and SAC makes payloads.

s: Which ISRO centre at Thiruvananthapuram is the lead centre for launch-vehicle design and development?
x: The Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Thiruvananthapuram leads launch-vehicle design and development.

s: Which ISRO unit tracks launch vehicles and satellites through its telemetry, tracking and command network?
x: ISTRAC, Bengaluru runs ISRO's telemetry, tracking and command network.

s: What was the earlier name of the U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC), Bengaluru?
x: URSC was earlier the ISRO Satellite Centre (ISAC); it is named after U.R. Rao.

s: What was the forerunner of the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad?
x: NRSC's forerunner was the National Remote Sensing Agency (NRSA).

s: Which of the following is NOT an overseas ISTRAC station?
x: Byalalu near Bengaluru hosts the Indian Deep Space Network; Mauritius, Brunei and Biak are overseas ISTRAC stations.

s: Where is the Indian Deep Space Network located?
x: The Indian Deep Space Network is at Byalalu near Bengaluru; Biak is an overseas ISTRAC station.

s: Under an ISRO-ESA Technical Implementing Plan, for which mission does ESA provide ground-tracking support?
x: The ISRO-ESA plan covers ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan.

s: Sriharikota Island lies near :

x: Sriharikota is now in Tirupati district; earlier it was in Nellore district.

o: Solid motors of sounding rockets only

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First launch pad — GSLV and LVM3
Second launch pad — PSLV and SSLV
First launch pad — PSLV and SSLV
Third launch pad — operational launch of PSLV-C62
x: C is correct: the first launch pad at Sriharikota handles PSLV and SSLV. A and B swap the pads (the second pad handles GSLV and LVM3 and is standby for PSLV). D is wrong: PSLV-C62 flew from the first launch pad; the Third Launch Pad is still to be built for NGLV.

s: Which of the following is NOT a reason supporting the selection of Sriharikota as a launch site?
o: Launches can proceed eastward over the sea.
The area is thinly populated and permits safe fall of spent stages.
The location benefits from the Earth's rotation.
It is located close to the northern polar region.
x: Sriharikota was selected because of its east-coast location, proximity to the equator, sea corridor for spent stages and relatively thin population. It is not close to the northern polar region.

s: For which launch vehicle is the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota, approved on 16 January 2025, meant?
x: The Third Launch Pad (Rs 3,984.86 crore, 48 months) is for NGLV; the first pad serves PSLV and SSLV.

s:
Consider the following statements about SDSC-SHAR, Sriharikota:
1. Its First Launch Pad serves PSLV and SSLV.
2. Its public Launch View Gallery opened in 2019.
3. It was renamed after Satish Dhawan in 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The First Launch Pad serves PSLV and SSLV and the gallery opened in 2019; SHAR was renamed after Dhawan in 2002, not 2012.

s: Sriharikota barrier island is situated between which of the following?
o: Kolleru Lake and the Arabian Sea
Pulicat Lake and the Bay of Bengal
Chilika Lake and the Indian Ocean
Vembanad Lake and the Bay of Bengal
x: Sriharikota lies between Pulicat Lake to the west and the Bay of Bengal to the east.

s: What was Sriharikota's launch centre called when it was set up in 1971?
x: It began in 1971 as the Sriharikota High Altitude Range (SHAR) and was renamed after Satish Dhawan in 2002.

s: Which mission marked the 100th launch from Sriharikota on 29 January 2025?
x: GSLV-F15 carrying NVS-02 (the 17th GSLV flight) was the 100th launch from SHAR.

s: What is the approved cost of the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota, cleared on 16 January 2025?
x: The Third Launch Pad was approved at Rs 3,984.86 crore, to be built in 48 months.

s: Within how many months is the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota to be completed?
x: The Third Launch Pad is to be built in 48 months; it will also be a standby for the second pad.

s: What is the main advantage of the Kulasekarapattinam launch complex for SSLV missions?
o: It is exclusively intended for launches of heavy-lift launch vehicles.
It permits direct southward launch into polar and sun-synchronous orbits without manoeuvring around Sri Lanka.
It is situated closer to the equator than Sriharikota and therefore eliminates all launch-cost constraints.
It enables launches directly into geostationary orbit without a cryogenic stage.
x: Kulasekarapattinam allows a direct southward trajectory into polar and sun-synchronous orbits, avoiding the fuel-costly manoeuvre around Sri Lanka required from Sriharikota.

s: The Kulasekarapattinam SSLV Launch Complex is in which district of Tamil Nadu?
x: It is in Thoothukudi (Tuticorin) district and is meant mainly for SSLV launches.
